title: ONE KEY EXPIRES... 10,000 REQUESTS?!
subtitle: Illustrative unprotected burst · same popular key
voiceover: Socho aapka system smooth chal raha tha, tabhi achanak Redis se ek single popular key expire ho jati hai. Ab agle hi microsecond mein 10,000 users wahi same data maangte hain. Redis ke paas data nahi hai — Cache Miss! Isse bolte hain Cache Stampede. Saari 10,000 requests ek sath seedhe Database par girti hain aur Database crash ho jata hai. Iska production fix hai Mutex Lock aur TTL Jitter.

title: REDIS CRASHED... ALL KEYS GONE!
subtitle: Cache Avalanche · Synchronized TTL Expiration
voiceover: Agar ek key expire hone par Cache Stampede hota hai, toh socho agar poora cache cluster ek sath khali ho jaye toh kya hoga? Isse bolte hain Cache Avalanche. Jab aap bulk warm-up karte hain same TTL ke sath, toh laakhon keys theek 1 ghante baad ek hi second mein expire ho jati hain. Result? Poora traffic database par girta hai. Iska fix hai hamesha TTL mein random jitter add karna.

title: BOT ATTACK: 50,000 HITS / SEC!
subtitle: Token Bucket Rate Limiting in Action
voiceover: Ek bot ne aapke login endpoint par per second 50,000 requests bhej di! Bina rate limiter ke aapka database turant choke ho jayega. Lekin Token Bucket algorithm ke sath, Redis Gateway par hi har client ko tokens assign karta hai. Jaise hi tokens khatam hue, 429 Too Many Requests return hota hai aur Database bilkul safe rehta hai.

title: ONE KEY EXPIRES... 10,000 REQUESTS?!
subtitle: Cache Stampede · Mutex Lock + Stale-While-Revalidate
voiceover: Socho aapka system normal chal raha tha, tabhi achanak Redis se ek single popular key expire ho jati hai. Ab agle hi microsecond mein 10,000 users wahi same data maangte hain. Redis ke paas data nahi hai — Cache Miss! Isse bolte hain Cache Stampede ya Thundering Herd! Saari 10,000 requests ek sath seedhe Database par girti hain aur Database crash ho jata hai. Isko rokne ke do best tareeqe hain: Pehla, Mutex Lock — sirf pehli request DB par jayegi aur baki 9,999 wait karengi. Dusra, Stale-While-Revalidate — puraana data turant serve karo aur background mein cache refresh karo. Pro tip: Apne cache TTL mein hamesha random jitter add karo taaki sabhi keys ek sath expire na hon.

title: KAFKA vs RABBITMQ
subtitle: Message padhne ke baad kahan jaata hai?
voiceover: Kafka aur RabbitMQ, dono message broker hain, lekin ek bada farak hai. Order service har order ko dono mein bhejti hai. Har order ek message hai. RabbitMQ message ko read hone ke baad delete kar deta hai. Kafka har message ko default 7 din tak rakhta hai. Ab ek naya service join hota hai, analytics ke liye. Kafka offset se purane messages ko replay kar sakta hai. RabbitMQ mein woh message ab bacha hi nahi. Email service dono ko process karti hai, aur har message ka ACK bhejti hai. Summary: data dobara chahiye to Kafka, aur task queue ke liye RabbitMQ.

title: CIRCUIT BREAKER
subtitle: Slow service ko bachane ka fuse

summary.text: Circuit breaker slow service ko bachata hai, aur user ko turant error deta hai.

voiceover: Socho ek payment service slow ho gaya hai, aur har request 10 second tak latak rahi hai. API gateway har request ko us service tak bhejti rehti hai, aur threads khatam hone lagte hain. Circuit breaker ek fuse ki tarah kaam karta hai. Failures ginne ke baad circuit OPEN ho jata hai. Ab requests API par hi fail fast ho jati hain, payment service par load nahi padta. Kuch der baad ek test request jati hai. Agar woh successful hai, to circuit wapas CLOSED ho jata hai. Summary: ye slow service ko bachata hai, aur user ko turant error deta hai.

subtitle: Postgres, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra

scenes.title: No joins
scenes.banner: QUERY KE HISAAB SE TABLE DESIGN KARO

scenes.title: Cache stampede
scenes.body: Agle video mein: cache stampede kaise rokein

voiceover: Database choose karna system design ka sabse bada decision hai. Postgres, MongoDB, Redis ya Cassandra, kaunsa lein? Maan lo ek food delivery app hai. Har order ka data kahin store hona chahiye: user, items, payment aur rider ka status. Database chunne se pehle 4 sawaal poocho. Structure kaisa hai? Read pattern kya hai? Write volume kitna hai? Aur galat choice ki cost kya hogi? In chaaron ke jawab se faisla ho jata hai. Postgres ek relational database hai. Isme tables, rows aur strict schema hote hain, aur complex queries ke liye best hai. Jab data ke beech relation important ho, tab ye sahi choice hai. Transaction ka matlab hai, order, payment aur coupon teeno ek saath ho ya koi nahi. Isko ACID kehte hain. Postgres ye guarantee deta hai, isliye paise aur orders ke liye ye safe hai. MongoDB ek document database hai. Data JSON jaise documents mein store hota hai, aur har document ka structure alag ho sakta hai. Redis ek key-value store hai. Data RAM mein rehta hai, isliye response time microseconds mein aata hai. Session aur cart jaise chhote data ke liye ye perfect hai. Isliye Redis super fast hai, hot data ke liye, jaise cache aur sessions. Lekin RAM mahanga hai aur limited bhi hai. Source of truth hamesha persistent database mein rakho. Cassandra wide-column database hai, jo writes ke liye bana hai. Isme koi single leader nahi hota, har node equal hai. Isliye ek node down ho jaye to bhi writes chalte rehte hain. Lekin Cassandra mein joins nahi hote, isliye table ko query ke hisaab se design karna padta hai. Summary: Postgres relations aur transactions ke liye, MongoDB flexible documents ke liye, Redis fast cache ke liye, aur Cassandra heavy writes ke liye. Ye faisla use case se hota hai. Agle video mein dekhenge cache stampede kaise rokein. Follow karo, aur batao aapka favourite database kaunsa hai.

title: POSTGRES vs REDIS vs CASSANDRA
subtitle: Kaunsa kab chalta hai

visual_timeline.details: Node 3 DOWN · traffic doosre nodes par reroute

voiceover: Postgres, Redis aur Cassandra, teeno ka kaam alag hai. Chaliye dekhte hain kaunsa kab chalta hai. Postgres mein ACID transaction milta hai, yaani data hamesha consistent rehta hai. Redis data RAM mein rakhta hai, isliye latency sirf point two milliseconds hai. Cassandra wide-column database hai, aur heavy writes ke liye bana hai. Ek node down ho jaye, to traffic doosre nodes par reroute ho jata hai. Summary: relations ke liye Postgres, speed ke liye Redis, aur heavy writes ke liye Cassandra.

scenes.title: TTL Jitter
scenes.body: TTL mein random ±10% add karo, taaki keys ek saath expire na hon.

voiceover: Socho aapka system normal chal raha hai. Har second sau requests aati hain, sab green signal par. Tabhi Redis ki ek popular key ka TTL zero ho jata hai, aur wo expire ho jati hai. Agle hi microsecond mein das hazaar users wahi key maangte hain, ek flood ki tarah. Cache miss hote hi saari requests seedhe database par girti hain, aur database crash ho jata hai. Fix: ek Mutex Lock. Lock lene ke liye SETNX command use hota hai. Sirf pehli request database tak jaati hai, baaki sab line mein wait karti hain. Pehli request data laati hai aur Redis ko refresh karti hai. Phir door wapas green, aur saari 9,999 requests instant serve hoti hain. Pro tip: TTL mein random jitter add karo, taaki keys ek saath expire na hon.
